intro: Ready-made pieces for your story. Your agent builds your blockout from these flat placeholder props and camera moves, so a new 30-second story takes minutes, not an hour.

sections.title: Shot sheet presets
sections.note: 21 presets for shot sheets (tools/previs). Each keeps the subject in frame. You can also save and reuse your own moves in the editor.

items.name: Locked wide
items.text: A fixed wide lens that sets the scene.
items.use: Opening or establishing a place; any time the audience needs to see where everything is.
items.long: A camera that does not move, placed back and to the side of where the subject is when the shot starts, wide enough to show the place around it. Push adds a slight creep in; look and mix lean the aim toward a second thing.

items.name: Face close, profile
items.text: Right beside the face, a little lead room ahead of the eyes.
items.use: An emotional beat while the subject moves: effort, fear, a decision.
items.long: Rides right beside the face at head height, with a little lead room ahead of the eyes so the move reads as forward.

items.name: Face close, front
items.text: On the line of travel, looking back at the face.
items.use: A reaction: the face as something happens behind it.
items.long: In front on the line of travel, backing up at the same speed and looking back at the face.

items.name: Over the shoulder
items.text: Close behind his back, the chase behind him.
items.use: Showing what the subject is chasing or running from.
items.long: Close behind the back, over one shoulder, looking down the road ahead; the subject stays big at one side of the frame.

items.name: Low chase
items.text: Low behind the subject, speed from the ground.
items.use: Speed and danger in a chase.
items.long: Behind and to one side at wheel height, following; the ground rushing past sells the speed.

items.name: Crane high
items.text: High wide shot with a slow push-in.
items.use: A breather between action beats, or to show the layout of a chase.
items.long: High behind the subject with a slow push-in and down, so the frame narrows onto it.

items.name: Side tracking
items.text: Alongside at wheel height.
items.use: Clean, readable motion; races and side-by-side moments.
items.long: Alongside at wheel height, matching speed, so the subject stays put while the world slides.

items.name: Front low tracking
items.text: Handlebar height, the subject comes at the lens.
items.use: A hero coming at the audience.
items.long: In front at handlebar height, backing up as the subject drives at the lens.

items.name: Front wide
items.text: In front and wide, backing away as they come.
items.use: Showing what is ahead and the subject at once.
items.long: In front on the line of travel and wide, backing away and rising a little as they come.

items.name: Worm's-eye
items.text: From the ground looking up, for leaps and slow motion.
items.use: Leaps, jumps and slow-motion hero moments.
items.long: From the ground looking up, so the subject passes over the lens against the sky.

items.name: Top-down
items.text: Straight overhead, the action as a diagram.
items.use: Making a chase or a near-miss readable as a diagram.
items.long: Straight overhead, optionally following; the action becomes shapes on a map.

items.name: Wheel close
items.text: On the wheel or handlebar, pure speed.
items.use: Pure speed inserts between wider shots.
items.long: Right on the wheel or the handlebar, very close and wide.

items.name: First-person
items.text: From the subject's own eyes, through tunnels and alleys.
items.use: Tunnels, alleys and anything the audience should live through.
items.long: From the subject's own eyes, moving with it.

items.name: Aerial spiral
items.text: Circling up and back to reveal the place.
items.use: Revealing a place, or the start and end of a sequence.
items.long: Circles up and back from the front while the radius and height grow.

items.name: Aerial pull-back
items.text: A held, symmetric pull-back for the ending.
items.use: The ending.
items.long: A held, symmetric pull-back that rises and leaves the subject small in the place.

items.name: Quarter close
items.text: A close three-quarter rear view.
items.use: Following close with a little more context than a back view.
items.long: A close three-quarter rear view that keeps the subject and its direction both readable.

items.name: Orbit
items.text: A bullet-time style circle around the subject.
items.use: A frozen or slow-motion moment, bullet time.
items.long: Circles the subject at a fixed radius and height through a set sweep.

items.name: Snorricam
items.text: Fixed to the body, the world shakes behind.
items.use: Panic, drunkenness, disorientation.
items.long: Mounted on the body facing the subject, so it stays still while the world swings behind.

items.name: Crash zoom
items.text: A fast punch-in on the moment.
items.use: A punchline or a sudden discovery.
items.long: A fixed camera whose lens punches in fast at one moment of the shot.

items.name: Dolly zoom
items.text: Pull back while zooming in, the background warps.
items.use: Realisation, vertigo, the world shifting.
items.long: Pulls back while the lens zooms in, so the subject keeps its size and the background stretches.

items.name: Hero low arc
items.text: A low arc round a hero, looking up.
items.use: A hero moment as the subject passes.
items.long: Low beside the subject, arcing round from the side to the front.

sections.title: Placeholder props
sections.note: Flat boxes and spheres. Colour carries identity to Seedance. Placed in a world file with PROPS.* (tools/previs/lib/props.js).

items.name: Building
items.text: A plain beige box.
items.use: Blocks for any town or city; streets are rows of them.
items.long: PROPS.building(x, z, w, h, d, hex) adds a beige box standing on the ground at x, z. PROPS.street(z0, z1) lines a whole road with them.

items.name: Tree
items.text: A trunk and a sphere.
items.use: Parks, roadsides and anything that should read as nature.
items.long: A brown trunk and a green sphere, scaled with s.

items.name: Street lamp
items.text: A thin box with a light.
items.use: Night streets: the light pools give the shot rhythm.
items.long: A thin pole with a warm light; sx = which side of the road it leans to.

items.name: Car
items.text: A box with wheels, any colour.
items.use: Traffic, parked cars, a taxi or a police car.
items.long: A box body with four wheels. taxi and cop switch the roof sign.

items.name: Bike
items.text: A red bike with a rider on it.
items.use: The hero vehicle of a chase.
items.long: A red bike with a rider pill and a package on the back.

items.name: Person (pill)
items.text: A capsule with a facing marker, no limbs.
items.use: Any character: the facing mark tells Seedance where they look.
items.long: A capsule with a facing marker, no limbs. Make people while the world is built, then move them in placeActors(t).

items.name: Bridge
items.text: Two leaves that rise.
items.use: A drawbridge jump or a closing-gap moment.
items.long: One leaf of a bascule bridge that can rise; two leaves make the bridge.

items.name: Tunnel
items.text: A dark shell with light strips.
items.use: A chase through the dark with light strips flashing past.
items.long: A dark shell along z with light strips on the ceiling.

items.name: Ramp and helipad
items.text: A tilted box and a flat disc.
items.use: Jumps and landings on roofs.
items.long: A tilted box (ramp) and a flat disc (helipad).

items.name: Clock tower
items.text: A tall box with a dial and moving hands.
items.use: A deadline everyone can read.
items.long: A tall box with a dial and moving hands.

items.name: Smoke
items.text: White spheres that Seedance turns into smoke.
items.use: Crashes, exhausts, explosions.
items.long: White spheres in one instanced mesh; move them every frame with set(i, position, radius). Seedance turns them into smoke.

items.name: Water
items.text: Light-blue spheres for a splash.
items.use: Splashes and puddles.
items.long: Light-blue spheres that Seedance reads as water.

items.name: Fruit
items.text: Orange spheres for flying fruit.
items.use: A stall knocked over, anything that should fly apart.
items.long: Orange spheres that Seedance reads as fruit.

items.name: Farm set
items.text: Barn, silo, hay bales, fence and a news van.
items.use: Rural stories: the aliens farm.
items.long: Barn, silo, hay bales and a fence.

items.name: Street POV
items.text: One take: an eagle, a skater and a donut, from a waterfall to the harbour.
items.use: Learning the editor on a one-take move.
items.long: One take: an eagle, a skater and a donut, from a waterfall to the harbour. Open it in the editor from Recent projects, or with the link below.

items.name: Any second now
items.text: A news crew at dusk, a farmer and a UFO. Five shots, four hard cuts.
items.use: A dialogue scene with hard cuts.
items.long: A news crew at dusk, a farmer and a UFO. Five shots, four hard cuts. Open it in the editor from Recent projects, or with the link below.

items.name: Midnight Courier
items.text: A courier on a red bike races an SUV over a drawbridge. 11 shots, 10 hard cuts.
items.use: A chase with cuts, slow motion, tracking and focus pulls.
items.long: A courier on a red bike races an SUV over a drawbridge. 11 shots, 10 hard cuts. Open it in the editor from Recent projects, or with the link below.

items.name: Midnight Courier 2
items.text: The same chase, re-cut: 20 shots, 19 hard cuts, slow-motion jump, face close-ups, a pulling-out finish.
items.use: Notes, Fix and Assist on a finished chase: try Review my shots.
items.long: The same chase, re-cut: 20 shots, 19 hard cuts, slow-motion jump, face close-ups, a pulling-out finish. Open it in the editor from Recent projects, or with the link below.

footer: Write a shot sheet in `tools/previs/` and run one command to build a story. Start with `tools/previs/README.md`.

paths.title: Camera paths
paths.note: Copy one, or add it to your moves and apply it to any shot in the editor (M).
